h1: The 6 Best Cordless Phones With Intercoms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Intercom Cordless Phones: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless phones with handset-to-handset intercom, compared on handset count, range, Bluetooth and call blocking.
summary: The Panasonic KX-TGD864W is the best overall, with four handsets, Link2Cell Bluetooth, a voice assistant and call blocking. The VTech IS8151-5 suits large properties with five handsets, a listed 2300 ft range and power backup. The AT&T BL102-4 is the four-handset value, and the DL72319 adds cell linking cheaply. The VTech VG232 kits are easiest to read.
intro: An intercom is only as useful as the number of handsets on the other end. Two handsets give you one conversation path, while four or five let you page the whole house from the kitchen or call the basement without shouting. That is why handset count, more than any other feature, drives the price of these systems, and why the right pick depends on how many rooms you genuinely want to reach.

Our editors reviewed six DECT 6.0 systems and ranked them on handset count, call handling features and fit for different households. Bluetooth cell linking, power backup, listed range and readability of the display all fed the Primea score. Bigger is not always better, and a two-handset kit suits a small flat better than a five-handset one.

products.name: Panasonic Cordless Phone with Answering Machine, Link2Cell Bluetooth Home Phones, Voice Assistant and Advanced Call Blocking, Expandable System with 4 Handsets, Cordless Telephone - KX-TGD864W
products.verdict: Four handsets plus Bluetooth, a voice assistant and call blocking.
products.description:
The KX-TGD864W stacks features on a four handset intercom. Link2Cell Bluetooth rings a paired mobile on every home handset, so cell calls reach you in the kitchen, and a voice assistant lets you talk to your phone through the base. Advanced call blocking filters spam before it rings.

It takes first place because it combines those extras with four handsets and an answering machine, while the VTech VG232-4 matches only the handset count. The VTech IS8151-5 adds range and power backup, but the Panasonic lists neither.

Buy it for a family home that wants intercom and cell linking. It lands in the $100 to $200 bucket, and a four handset system is more than a small flat needs.
cons: More than a small home needs
products.idealFor: Family homes that want intercom plus cell linking.

products.name: VTech IS8151-5 Super Long Range 5 Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, 2300 ft Range, Call Blocking, Bluetooth, Headset Jack, Power Backup, Intercom, Expandable to 12 HS
products.verdict: Five handsets, 2300 ft range and power backup.
products.description:
The IS8151-5 is built for distance. It ships with five handsets, lists a 2300 ft range, and expands to 12 handsets, which covers a garage, workshop or guest cabin. Power backup keeps a handset working in an outage, a feature the Panasonic does not list, and a headset jack suits long calls.

It ranks second because the Panasonic carries the better extras for everyday use, and range figures like 2300 ft describe open air. Indoors, walls and floors cut that sharply.

Buy it for a large house, a farm or a property with outbuildings. Skip it in an apartment, where five handsets and that range are wasted. The system also lists Bluetooth, but the Panasonic's cell integration is the more polished.

products.name: AT&T BL102-4 DECT 6.0 4-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Four handsets with call blocking and caller ID announcer.
products.description:
The BL102-4 delivers the essentials in a four handset kit: answering machine, call blocking, a caller ID announcer that speaks the name aloud, and audio assist, which boosts volume on a weak line. These matter more day to day than a long feature sheet.

It ranks third because it has no Bluetooth or voice assistant, both of which the Panasonic includes. It sits in the same $100 to $200 bucket, so the Panasonic is the better buy if you want cell linking.

Buy it for a larger home that wants call blocking and an announcer without paying for cell integration. The caveat is that cell calls will not ring on the handsets, so you still answer your mobile separately. A household without a landline would find less value here.
products.idealFor: Larger homes focused on core calling.

products.award: Best Cell Link on a Budget
products.name: AT&T DL72319 DECT 6.0 3-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Connect to Cell, Call Blocking, 1.8" Backlit Screen, Big Buttons, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Connect to Cell with three handsets for less.
products.description:
The DL72319 puts cell linking in a budget kit. Connect to Cell pairs a mobile to the base, so calls reach three handsets with intercom between them, and call blocking trims spam. Big buttons and a 1.8 inch backlit screen keep dialing simple.

It ranks fourth because three handsets cover a mid-sized home, but the BL102-4 provides a fourth and an answering machine, which this listing does not mention. At the $50 to $100 bucket it undercuts both AT&T four handset kits.

Buy it if cell signal is weak at home and you want your mobile to ring on landline handsets. The caveat: the 1.8 inch screen is small, and without a stated answering machine you need voicemail from your carrier.
products.idealFor: Mid-sized homes that take cell calls at home.
products.skipIf: You rely on an answering machine.

products.name: VTech Cordless Phone with 4 Handsets, Big Buttons, Large Backlit Display, Answering Machine, DECT 6.0, Whole-Home Coverage, Intercom, Easy to Use - VG232-4
products.verdict: Four easy-to-read handsets and whole-home coverage.
products.description:
The VG232-4 is the easy-to-read four handset kit. Big buttons and a large backlit display suit older eyes, an answering machine handles missed calls, and whole-home coverage reaches across a normal house. Four handsets in the $50 to $100 bucket make it the cheapest route to a four-room intercom.

It ranks fifth because the listing skips call blocking and Bluetooth, which the Panasonic and BL102-4 both offer. Spam calls will ring through unless your carrier filters them.

Buy it for households with older users who need clear buttons and screens. Skip it if spam is a daily nuisance. The system is expandable, but you must buy matching VTech handsets, so check compatibility before adding any.

products.name: VTech Cordless Phone with 2 Handsets, Big Buttons, Large Backlit Display, Answering Machine, DECT 6.0, Caller ID, Intercom, Easy to Use, Silver/Black - VG232-2
products.verdict: The simplest way to get an intercom between two rooms.
products.description:
The VG232-2 is the simplest intercom in the ranking. Two handsets, big buttons, a large backlit display, an answering machine and caller ID cover a small home. Two handsets are the minimum an intercom needs, giving one path between two rooms.

It ranks last because it lacks the call blocking that AT&T's kits include, and two handsets limit reach. It is also the lowest price here, in the $50 to $100 bucket, which is its draw.

Buy it for a small flat or house where you only need to page between two rooms. Skip it if you need more than two handsets or live with relentless spam. The caveat is expansion: adding more VTech handsets later costs more than starting with the four handset VG232-4.
products.idealFor: Small homes paging between two rooms.
products.skipIf: You need more than two handsets.

whatMatters.detail: An intercom connects handsets to each other, so the count decides how many rooms you can reach. Two handsets give one path, while four or five let you page a household or call the basement. Check the handset number in the title, and confirm it counts included handsets, not the maximum the base can support. Extra handsets bought later cost more per unit.

Range is how far a handset can roam from the base before it drops out. Walls, floors and appliances reduce it sharply, so open-air figures overstate real use. The IS8151-5 lists 2300 ft, which is open air. Look for a feet figure in the title, and assume indoor range is a fraction of it, especially through brick or concrete.

Link2Cell and Connect to Cell pair a mobile phone to the base by Bluetooth so cell calls ring on home handsets. That helps where cell signal is poor indoors and lets every room answer. Look for those exact names, or Bluetooth, on the listing. Without them, the system handles only landline calls, and your mobile stays separate.

Most cordless bases lose power in an outage, which silences every handset. Power backup keeps at least one handset alive on batteries or a backup source. It matters if the phone is your emergency line, and it keeps one handset alive during a cut. Check the listing for the phrase power backup, which only the IS8151-5 states among these picks. A corded phone is the only other safe fallback.

Call blocking stops flagged or unwanted numbers from ringing through, which matters for homes that get frequent spam. Some systems store numbers you add, others use a list. Look for the phrase call blocking or advanced call blocking on the listing. The VG232 kits do not state it, so spam rings through unless your carrier filters it.

faq.q: How does a cordless phone intercom work?
faq.a: It lets one handset call another through the base without using the phone line. You press the intercom key, choose the handset, and speak. The VG232-4 and BL102-4 both work this way across four handsets.

Many systems are expandable, such as the IS8151-5 up to 12 handsets. Buy matching handsets that are compatible with your base, since mixing brands or DECT generations often fails, and a wrong handset may refuse to register.

Only if you take cell calls at home or have weak signal indoors. The KX-TGD864W and DL72319 add cell linking. Otherwise it adds cost to the system without much benefit, since a mobile can stay in your pocket.

faq.q: How do I use the intercom?
faq.a: Press the intercom key on one handset and choose another. Some systems, including the AT&T BL102-4, can also page all handsets at once, which suits calling the household to dinner or a quick warning from the front door.

faq.q: How far will the intercom reach?
faq.a: It depends on walls and floors. The IS8151-5 lists 2300 ft in open air, but expect much less indoors, particularly through masonry or across floors. For a standard house, any DECT 6.0 kit here is fine, and the IS8151-5 matters only on large plots.

faq.q: Do these phones work during a power cut?
faq.a: Most do not, because the base needs mains power. The VTech IS8151-5 lists power backup, so it is the one to consider if the phone is your emergency line.

finalTake: Buy the Panasonic KX-TGD864W if you want intercom plus cell linking in a family home, and the VTech IS8151-5 for acreage or outbuildings. The AT&T BL102-4 covers core calling for less. Choose a VG232 kit for older users or a small home, and skip Bluetooth unless you take cell calls inside.
